rule: One name, one contract: a name two packages export is the same object in both, or it is listed under shared_names with the reason the two are deliberately different.

Bar.reason: Wire and domain: data.feed.Bar is an OHLCV aggregate as a provider reported it (a provider symbol, float prices); market.bar.Bar is the domain bar the execution path consumes (an asset id, Decimal prices, an optional vwap and trade count). One is converted into the other at ingestion; they sit on opposite sides of that conversion.

CashFlow.reason: Two cash flows of two instruments: macro.bond.CashFlow is one payment a bond's schedule makes; portfolio.corporate_actions.CashFlow is cash a holding earned or cost without a trade (a dividend, a fee) booked to an account.

Dataset.reason: A canonical price series and a design matrix: data.dataset.Dataset is one immutable, versioned dataset of market records; ml.dataset.Dataset is features and a target ready for a model. Section 13 of the shared-names test.

ExposureUpdated.reason: Two engines' notifications: risk.events.ExposureUpdated carries the gross and net exposure the pre-trade gate computed and is persisted under the risk event tags; portfolio_optimizer.events.ExposureUpdated says a constructed portfolio's exposure was recomputed. Renaming the persisted one is a format change (tests/regression/test_persisted_enum_names.py).

InvalidTransitionError.reason: Each state machine's own refusal, under its own package's error base: oms.exceptions.InvalidTransitionError for an order's lifecycle, strategy.exceptions.InvalidTransitionError for a strategy instance's. Catching one deliberately does not catch the other.

MarketDataError.reason: Each package's error base: market.exceptions.MarketDataError for the market data engine, marketdata.exceptions.MarketDataError for the transports that feed it.

OrderAccepted.reason: Two sides of one order: oms.events.OrderAccepted is the OMS's lifecycle transition; broker.events.OrderAccepted is a venue's acknowledgement, which the OMS may or may not then reflect. Each is persisted under its own subsystem's event tags, so neither can be renamed without a schema step.

OrderBook.reason: My working orders and the market's resting size: oms.book.OrderBook indexes the OMS's own orders; data.feed.OrderBook is a provider's depth snapshot. They share no operation (tests/regression/test_shared_names_stay_distinct.py, section 1).

OrderBookLevel.reason: Wire and domain: data.feed.OrderBookLevel is one level of a provider's depth record (no order count); market.level.OrderBookLevel is the domain level of a market book snapshot.

OrderCancelled.reason: The OMS's lifecycle transition and a venue's cancel confirmation: two events, each persisted under its own subsystem's tags. See OrderAccepted.

OrderId.reason: Two representations of one identity across one boundary: core.ids.OrderId is the text a fill and a trade record carry and a payload persists; oms.ids.OrderId is the OMS's typed key, a UUID whose hash is computed once (ledger PRF-006). The runtime converts between them in alphalab.runtime.execution_adapters.

OrderRejected.reason: The OMS's refusal of an order and a venue's: two events, each persisted under its own subsystem's tags. See OrderAccepted.

OrderSubmitted.reason: The OMS's record that an order was submitted and the broker boundary's record that it reached a venue: two events, each persisted under its own subsystem's tags. See OrderAccepted.

PortfolioEngine.reason: Accounting and construction: portfolio.PortfolioEngine keeps the book from fills; portfolio_optimizer.PortfolioEngine assembles target weights. Only the first is reachable from the execution path. Section 2 of the shared-names test.

PortfolioEvent.reason: Each engine's event base: portfolio.events.PortfolioEvent is the base of what the accounting book records, and its subclasses are persisted under the portfolio event tags; portfolio_optimizer.events.PortfolioEvent is the construction engine's base, which no snapshot carries.

Quote.reason: Wire and domain: data.feed.Quote is a provider's top of book as reported (a provider symbol, floats); market.quote.Quote is the domain quote the execution path consumes (an asset id, Decimals, a venue and a currency). Converted at ingestion.

ReportGenerated.reason: Two reports: analytics.events.ReportGenerated is a performance report compiled on the execution path and persisted under the analytics event tags; reporting.events.ReportGenerated is a document the reporting engine rendered and stored.

SessionCalendar.reason: Two narrow protocols, each stating only what its reader needs from a calendar: alt_data's places an instant in a trading day (is_open, next_open, session windows), futures' only asks whether a day is a trading day, for a roll rule. data.calendar.MarketCalendar satisfies both; neither is a calendar. Section 19 of the shared-names test.

Split.reason: Wire and domain: data.feed.Split is a split as a corporate-action feed reports it (symbol, ratio as a float); portfolio.corporate_actions.Split is the action applied to a holding, which also expresses a reverse split and a stock dividend exactly.

Trade.reason: Two different trades: core.trade.Trade is an execution AlphaLab's own order made, as the accounting records it; data.feed.Trade is a print a provider reported on the tape, anyone's.

all_reports.reason: Each package's view over its own state: analytics.all_reports(AnalyticsState) returns performance reports, execution.all_reports(ExecutionState) execution reports. The state argument says which.

checkpoint.reason: Two checkpoints of two states: runtime.checkpoint(RunState, previous) writes the next incremental checkpoint of a run; strategy.checkpoint(AdaptiveState) gives a learned state's primitives. The argument says which.

compare_runs.reason: Two comparisons: experiment_tracking.compare_runs reads one metric across tracked runs; lifecycle.compare_runs compares two runs' observations metric by metric under declared tolerances. Different arguments, different results.

compute_pnl.reason: Each instrument's own P&L: futures.compute_pnl(CalendarSpread, ...) for a calendar spread, options.compute_pnl(OptionStrategy, ...) for an options strategy at a spot price.

factor_exposure.reason: A book's and a weighting's: analytics.factor_exposure weights positions' factor loadings; factor_library.factor_exposure aggregates a weighting's exposure by asset and group. Section 39 of the shared-names test.

list_versions.reason: Each registry's own versions: feature_store.list_versions(FeatureStoreState, feature_id) and model_registry.list_versions(ModelRegistry, name).

register_strategy.reason: Two registrations: lifecycle.register_strategy records a strategy *version* in the lifecycle registry, checking what it cites; strategy.register_strategy adds a strategy *instance* to a running session.

restore.reason: Two restorations of two states: oms.restore(OMSSnapshot) rebuilds the OMS state from its snapshot; strategy.restore(payload, configuration, rule) rebuilds an adaptive state from strategy.checkpoint's primitives, or refuses.

rollback.reason: Two rollbacks: deployment_manager.rollback re-deploys an environment's previous release; model_registry.rollback archives a model's production version and restores the one before.

spread.reason: Two spreads: macro.spread is a yield curve's long-tenor minus short-tenor yield; market.spread is an order book's best ask minus best bid.

surprise.reason: Two surprises: macro.surprise is an indicator's actual minus its recorded consensus; alt_data.surprise is the difference between two measurements an information event carries, which the caller names.
